_exec_summary.SummaryText:
Empirical foods, inc. will operate as a meat processing facility for food products used for human consumption.  The SIC code for the operating plant will be 2013; the NAICS code is 311612. This facility has approximately 150 full time employees. At the time of this submission the facility is under construction but plans to be operational by the end of 2025. 
I. The facility has developed a Process Safety Management Program (PSM) in accordance with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Standard 29CFR 1910.119 and the Environmental Protection Agency's Risk Management Program 40 CFR 68 as their accidental release prevention program.  The system is continuously monitored by computer based controls that alert technicians that are trained, qualified, and experienced in ammonia refrigeration and process systems in accordance with the facilities PSM/RMP program. The system is visually inspected periodically for proper daily operation. System parameters are digitally logged into the PLC system. Safe operation of the system will be accomplished by utilizing general good operating procedures and providing appropriate training to employees.
This facility has developed and implemented a written Emergency Action Plan as defined by 29CFR 1910.38 as their emergency response program. Emergency evacuation drills are conducted on a periodic basis to ensure personnel quickly and safely evacuate the plant. This facility will utilize outside agencies and/or organizations to perform emergency response measures in the event of a fire, explosion, or hazardous material release.

II. Description of the Stationary Source and Regulated Substances handled:

Our single process chemical is Anhydrous Ammonia.  Ammonia is used in two processes within the facility, the Ammonia Refrigeration System and as a processing aid in the Process Ammonia System. 
The refrigeration system is a closed loop refrigeration system that the facility used to keep product and facility processing areas

at target temperatures to preserve food safety standards. The major components of the ammonia refrigeration system are located in the machinery rooms.
The Process Ammonia system converts food grade anhydrous ammonia to ammonia hydroxide, and uses it as a processing aid in the production of beef products at the facility. This process is an approved antimicrobial treatment by the USDA food safety inspection service. The ammonia used for this purpose is stored separately from the refrigeration  system but operate in close proximity to each other.
Support operations include a maintenance shop, parts warehouse and administrative offices.
Anhydrous ammonia is listed as a hazardous chemical subject to the RMP regulation with a threshold quantity of 10,000 lbs.  The operating capacity of this system exceeds this thresehold.

III. General Accidental Release Prevention program and Chemical Specific Prevention Steps:

This facility complies with the provisions of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration's Process Safety Management Program 29 CFR 68. The facilities PSM program includes provisions for Process Hazard Analysis, management of change, pre-startup safety reviews, safety work practices, inspections, testing, maintenance, compliance audits, and contractor qualifications. Qualified outside contractors are used for construction and major repairs or modifications to the system.  The the PSM/RMP program will be reviewed annually and updated as necessary.  All significant changes to the system are previewed in accordance with the PSM/RMP management of change provisions stated in the facilities plan.
The ammonia system is controlled and monitored 24/7 by an Operations Center at a remote location. The system is equipped with a series of redundant fail safe devices, sensors, and overrides. In the event a malfunction occurs that could result in an ammonia release, these protective devices will shut down the system. The system can not be restarted until the cause of th

e shutdown is identified and corrected.  The system is equipped with ammonia detectors that alarm and start local emergency ventilation system with the presence of ammonia is sensed above set point levels in the machinery room. The system can be shut down remotely or by using an emergency shutdown switch located outside of the machinery room exits.

IV.  Fire Year Accident History
This is a new facility being built and has had no previous accidental releases.

V.  Emergency Response Program
The facility is making arrangements with the local Fire Department and LEPC to respond to emergencies involving anhydrous ammonia.  The facility plans to conduct periodic site visits with local emergency responders and conducts annual evacuation drills with employee and contractors onsite.
The facilities emergency action plan includes procedures for notifying the proper Federal, State, and local agencies in the event of a reportable release of ammonia.

VI.  Planned Changes to Improve Safety
The facility will upgrade and update safety programs as needed.
